stem: A bank offers a nominal interest rate of 12% per annum, compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate of interest? [Use: (1.01) raised to the power 12 = 1.1268]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Effective rate = (1 + 0.12/12) raised to the power 12 - 1 = (1.01) raised to the power 12 - 1 = 1.1268 - 1 = 0.1268 = 12.68%.
Student treats the nominal rate as the effective rate, ignoring compounding within the year.
Student uses (1 + 0.12/2)² - 1, treating monthly compounding as semi-annual: (1.06)² - 1 = 0.1236.
Student computes 1.1268 - 1.01 = 0.1168, subtracting one monthly factor instead of 1.

explanation: Effective annual rate = (1 + r/m)^m - 1, where r = 0.12 and m = 12. This gives (1.01) raised to the power 12 - 1 = 1.1268 - 1 = 12.68%. The nominal rate 12% ignores within-year compounding, so it understates the true cost.
